narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Reads all narration, speech introductions and glosses on names.

angel.name: The man who wrestles with Jacob
angel.note: The mysterious wrestler at the ford of Jaboc; terse, withholding his name, then blessing.

jacob.name: Jacob
jacob.note: The patriarch returning from Mesopotamia; aggrieved with Laban, fearful and deferential before Esau, commanding with his household.

messengers.name: Jacob's messengers
messengers.note: Servants reporting back that Esau approaches; urgent.

1.t: Jacob also went on the journey he had begun: and the angels of God met him.

2.t: And when he saw them, he said:
These are the camps of God,
and he called the name of that place Mahanaim, that is, Camps.

3.t: And he sent messengers before him to Esau, his brother, to the land of Seir, to the country of Edom:

4.t: Thus shall ye speak to my lord Esau: Thus saith thy brother Jacob: I have sojourned with Laban, and have been with him until this day:

5.t: I have oxen, and asses, and sheep, and menservants, and womenservants: and now I send a message to my lord, that I may find favour in thy sight.

6.t: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying:
We came to Esau, thy brother, and behold he cometh with speed to meet thee with four hundred men.

7.t: Then Jacob was greatly afraid; and in his fear divided the people that was with him, and the flocks, and the sheep, and the oxen, and the camels, into two companies,

8.t: If Esau come to one company, and destroy it, the other company that is left, shall escape.
8.q: Jacob's reasoning, spoken or thought; given to his voice.

9.t: O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac: O Lord who saidst to me, Return to thy land, and to the place of thy birth, and I will do well for thee.

10.t: I am not worthy of the least of all thy mercies, and of thy truth which thou hast fulfilled to thy servant. With my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I return with two companies.

11.t: Deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am greatly afraid of him; lest perhaps he come, and kill the mother with the children.

12.t: Thou didst say, that thou wouldst do well by me, and multiply my seed like the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.

13.t: And when he had slept there that night, he set apart, of the things which he had, presents for his brother Esau,

14.t: Two hundred she-goats, twenty he-goats, two hundred ewes, and twenty rams,

15.t: Thirty milch camels with their colts, forty kine, and twenty bulls, twenty she-asses, and ten of their foals.

16.t: And he sent them by the hands of his servants, every drove by itself, and he said to his servants:
Go before me, and let there be a space between drove and drove.

17.t: And he commanded the first, saying:
If thou meet my brother Esau, and he ask thee: Whose art thou? or whither goest thou? or whose are these before thee?

18.t: Thou shalt answer: Thy servant Jacob's: he hath sent them as a present to my lord Esau; and he cometh after us.

19.t: In like manner he commanded the second, and the third, and all that followed the droves, saying:
Speak ye the same words to Esau, when ye find him.

20.t: And ye shall add: Thy servant Jacob himself also followeth after us; for he said: I will appease him with the presents that go before, and afterwards I will see him, perhaps he will be gracious to me.

21.t: So the presents went before him, but himself lodged that night in the camp.

22.t: And rising early, he took his two wives and his two handmaids, with his eleven sons, and passed over the ford of Jaboc.

23.t: And when all things were brought over that belonged to him,

24.t: He remained alone; and behold, a man wrestled with him till morning.

25.t: And when he saw that he could not overcome him, he touched the sinew of his thigh, and forthwith it shrank.

26.t: Let me go, for it is break of day.
I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.

28.t: Thy name shall not be called Jacob, but Israel; for if thou hast been strong against God, how much more shalt thou prevail against men?

29.t: Tell me by what name art thou called?
Why dost thou ask my name?
And he blessed him in the same place.

30.t: And Jacob called the name of the place Phanuel, saying:
I have seen God face to face, and my soul has been saved.

31.t: And immediately the sun rose upon him, after he was past Phanuel; but he halted on his foot.

32.t: Therefore the children of Israel, unto this day, eat not the sinew, that shrank in Jacob's thigh: because he touched the sinew of his thigh and it shrank.
